note: AutoCompact (arXiv 2610.02163v1, submitted 2026-10-01). Headline numbers on screen: 30.4% and 39.6%, SWE-bench Verified pass rates of the base model with its full 256K context (no learned compaction; no run reaches the forced-compaction threshold) and of AutoCompact (SFT then RL, 256K), full agent runs without a cost cap, averaged over three runs (Table 1, sec 3.1). 19.9 points and 1.9 points: absolute pass-rate differences between the same trained checkpoint running its compact() calls and skipping them, at the smallest ($0.10) and largest ($4.00) per-task budget (sec 3.3, Figure 3(d)); the paper writes them with a % sign, the video says points. All authors' runs, one base model (not named on screen) and one scaffold.

numbers.30.4: Base pass rate on SWE-bench Verified, 30.4% (Table 1 p.6, Base row, Context 256K; sec 1 p.2; Figure 3(a) label 30.4%). Average of three runs (sec 3.1). On screen in results (l09).
numbers.39.6: AutoCompact pass rate on SWE-bench Verified, 39.6% (Table 1 p.6, AutoCompact row, SFT then RL, 256K; sec 1 p.2 'achieving pass rates of 39.6%'; abstract +9.2 absolute). Average of three runs. On screen in results (l09).
numbers.19.9: Advantage of normal execution over the Summary-ignored variant (compact() calls skipped, same parameters) at $0.10 per task: 'The advantage is 19.9% at $0.10' (sec 3.3 p.8; Figure 3(d) +100 tasks per 500). Absolute difference in pass rate, shown as '19.9 points'. The largest gap of the six-budget sweep; l11 names the smallest budget. On screen in caveat (l11).
numbers.1.9: Same comparison at $4.00 per task: 'remains 1.9% at $4.00' (sec 3.3 p.8; Figure 3(d) endpoint labels 39.6% and 37.7%). Absolute difference, shown as '1.9 points'. The smallest gap of the sweep; l12 names the largest budget. On screen in caveat (l12).

numbers.3.3: Section number in the receipt tags 'FROM THE PAPER · Section 3.3' (l10, l11); sec 3.3 'Further analysis'.

claims.l01: Sec 5 Limitations (p.9): 'Widely used agent harnesses ... currently compact the context automatically when it approaches the window limit, which is the length-triggered design discussed in Section 1.' Sec 1 (p.1): length-triggered methods 'compact only when the remaining context budget falls below a fixed threshold'. 'Wrong moment?' stays a question; the paper's reason is l03. No product is named in the video.
claims.l02: Sec 2.1 (p.3): 'Compaction replaces earlier interaction history with a model-generated working-state summary ... while retaining the original task unchanged.' Card rows 'state, target file, next step' are the words of Figure 2.
claims.l03: Abstract (p.1), word for word: 'As a task progresses, earlier exploration becomes stale' (receipt R1, id stale). Sec 1 (p.1): 'compaction may then occur in the middle of an unresolved stage whose evidence is still needed.' The video says 'can', matching the paper's 'may'; no count of lost evidence is claimed.
claims.l04: Abstract and sec 1: AutoCompact 'trains a coding agent to decide when to compact, what to preserve, and how to continue as part of its policy'. Figure 1 header: 'decide when to compact, what to keep, and how to continue'.
claims.l05: Sec 2.2 (p.3): 'In our preliminary experiments, the base model rarely invoked compact() before the context limit, even when compaction rules were specified in the agent prompt.' Receipt R2 (id rarely).
claims.l06: Sec 2.2 (p.4): the judge reviews each proposed action using only the history available at the current step; 'Corrections are applied before execution'; the environment executes the corrected output 'in place of the original; the policy then generates the following actions from this corrected history.' Ghost label 'search repo' and fix 'compact()': Figure 2 (replacing a search after the bug is localized with compact()).
claims.l07: Sec 2.2 (p.4), continuation correction: 'such as re-running a search whose result is already recorded in the working-state summary'. Figure 2: 'Search repo again / ignores the summary', 'Repair / follow the summary', 'Edit file / continue from the summary'; caption: 'redirecting a repeated search toward the edit planned in the summary'.
claims.l08: Sec 2.2 (p.4): 'The judge is used only during data collection; the trained agent runs without the judge at inference time.' Sec 2.3 (p.4-5): each rollout receives a binary outcome reward (final patch passes the task tests); the shared advantage covers 'regular coding actions, the decision to invoke compact(), the generated context summary, and the continuation'; no compaction-specific reward; 'the binary outcome reward is the only training signal for both coding and compaction.' The SFT stage before RL is not narrated.
claims.l09: Table 1 (p.6): Base 30.4, AutoCompact 39.6 on SWE-bench Verified; caption 'All methods share the same base model and scaffold.' Sec 3.1: averaged over three runs, full agent runs without an inference-cost cap. 'Full context' = Base keeps the full history in a 256K window that no run fills (sec 1, Figure 3 caption). The 9.2-point gap is the whole SFT-then-RL recipe against an untrained base; l11 and l12 qualify it.
claims.l10: Sec 3.3 (p.7-8) and Figure 3(c): Base and AutoCompact under a shared 16K forced-compaction threshold; 'AutoCompact achieves a higher pass rate than Base across all evaluated inference budgets.' 'It also indicates that compaction based on task progress is more effective than compaction based solely on the length of the context.' (receipt R3, id progress). The voice attributes the second sentence to the authors.
claims.l11: Sec 3.3 (p.8): Summary-ignored variant of the same trained checkpoint, 'compact() calls are skipped: no summary is generated, and execution continues with the existing history'; 'Figure 3 (d) shows that normal execution achieves higher pass rates'; 'The advantage is 19.9% at $0.10' (receipt R4a, id adv1).
claims.l12: First sentence: sec 3.3 (p.8) 'The advantage is 19.9% at $0.10 and remains 1.9% at $4.00' (receipt R4b, id adv2); the advantage is normal execution over the Summary-ignored variant of the same checkpoint, as in l11. Second sentence restates sec 1 (p.2): 'Comparing the same trained checkpoint with and without executing compaction further shows that compaction is particularly beneficial under tight inference budgets'; sec 3.3: 'with the largest advantage under tight inference budgets'. The scene pulses the smallest-budget column (the largest gap, 19.9 points at $0.10). No claim is made about how much of the 9.2-point gain comes from training versus compaction. Tag 'one base model · one scaffold': sec 3.1 and sec 5 ('We study this co-design within a single scaffold').
